content:
Jamie L: Hey team — I pushed a first-pass AZ5 cluster onboarding playbook to the docs. Need a quick review focused on: GPU capacity checks, network ACLs, known issues, and the handoff checklist to Platform Ops. https://redwood.docs/internal/az5-onboard (draft)
Ravi P: Thanks! I'll skim for capacity/cost items. Do we have the SKU list for the initial pool?
Jamie L: yes — I added it under 'Provisioning -> GPU pool sizes' but worth a sanity check. TL;DR I'm proposing 4x A10x8 (32GB) nodes + 2x T4 fallback for burst.
Marta S: Quick note — AZ5 region has a weird quota shape for T4s, we might not get the full burst numbers. Need a fallback plan if stock is limited.
Kevin T: Can we add an autoscale policy snippet? Small one to go from 2 -> 20 pods with a 60s cooldown. Also put an explicit pod-disruption budget.
Jamie L: added an autoscale example. See snippet below (in doc):
```yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: inference-workers
spec:
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 20
  metrics:
    - type: Resource
      resource:
        name: cpu
        target:
          type: Utilization
          averageUtilization: 65
```
Ravi P: Looks good. For cost calc, add per-token projected spend with the A10 profile vs quantized fp16 profiles. Helps legal/finance signoff.
Jamie L: will do. Added a small table and a reference to Optimize recommendations.
Sophia H: On the networking side, the doc currently says "open SG for 10250" — can we be explicit: control-plane security group needs 10250 (kubelet), 6443 (api), 179 (BGP for CNI peering) and deny 0.0.0.0/0 egress where possible.
Marta S: +1. Also add a troubleshooting step for flapping routes we saw in AZ3: check CNI bfd timers and MTU mismatches.
Jamie L: added Known Issues section. I wrote two items: (1) intermittent pod scheduling delays because of quota checks, (2) degraded latency when KV cache warmup misses.
Kevin T: For (2) include quick mitigation: explicitly seed KV cache on rollout and set warmup requests to 5 replicas for 30s. Example command: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/inference && sleep 30 && for p in $(kubectl get pods -l app=inference -o name); do kubectl exec $p -- /app/seed_cache; done`
ops-bot: Validation run completed for doc link https://redwood.docs/internal/az5-onboard: spellcheck ok, links ok, YAML lint OK.
Ravi P: One more: handoff checklist for Platform Ops should include the capacity reservation ticket, KMS access confirmation, monitoring dashboards cloned, and a runbook page copied to the oncall binder.
Jamie L: added a handoff checklist. Draft checklist items:
- capacity reservation created (#OPS-4521)
- KMS key accessible to env prod-az5
- alert thresholds in cockpit: pod_cpu > 85% for 5m, request_queue > 50 for 2m
- canary traffic route + fallback policy verified
- post-deploy smoke test (endpoints returning 200 and sample inference under 200ms P95)
Marta S: For smoke tests, add a step to run an inference with 1k tokens so we measure long-tail perf.
Jamie L: done. Also added a short troubleshooting guide at the end with quick checks: node GPU health, nvml errors, kernel driver mismatch, rack power alerts, and CNI route table checks.
Sophia H: Recommend adding a 'what not to do' note: don't roll kubernetes kubelet and runtime simultaneously on all nodes — do one rack at a time.
Jamie L: good call, added.
Kevin T: LGTM overall. I'd like a short section about rollback criteria: if p95 latency increases > 40% for 10m or error rate > 3% for 5m, auto-failover to fallback model variant and page SRE.
Ravi P: I'll help finalize the cost/capacity appendix and run the quota request with cloud provider contacts.
Jamie L: Thanks everyone. Final ask: can Platform Ops (+Sophia) do a dry-run of the handoff checklist next week? If yes I'll mark doc Ready-for-Handoff.
Sophia H: I can do Tue 10am PT.
Marta S: I'll be there to watch the network checks.
Jamie L: Awesome — I'll update the doc status and link OPS ticket then. :tada:
